title: Costly Arbitrage: Evidence from Closed-End Funds
one_line: Closed-end fund discounts are larger and more persistent when arbitrage is costly — when the fund's holdings are hard to hedge (high idiosyncratic risk), dividends are low and interest rates high.

findings.statement: Mispricing size rises with idiosyncratic risk and holding costs.

why.pattern: Arbitrage costs determine how much mispricing survives.

reported_results.headline: Closed-end fund discounts are larger and more persistent when arbitrage is costly — when the fund's holdings are hard to hedge (high idiosyncratic risk), dividends are low and interest rates high.

data_fit: Single-stock study — not testable on our ES/NQ data.
